headline: S&P 500 closed at 7,543.59 on softer-than-expected CPI; futures near flat pre-market as PPI, Warsh Day-2 testimony, and a wave of earnings take center stage.
stance: Constructive but alert. Yesterday's CPI beat gave equities a lift led by semiconductors and big-bank beats, yet the 10-year yield (prior close 4.58%) and a still-elevated real rate of 2.33% keep the cost-of-money headwind alive. Today's PPI print and Warsh's second congressional appearance are the swing factors — a second consecutive downside inflation surprise could meaningfully reduce the ~50% market-implied probability of a September Fed hike, while a hawkish Warsh tone could reverse it.

news.head: CPI Surprise — Inflation Cools
news.body: June CPI came in at 3.5% year-over-year (down from 4.2% in May), with consumer prices falling 0.4% month-over-month — the first monthly decline since 2020 — and core CPI slowing to 2.6%, both below forecasts.

news.head: Big-Bank Earnings Sweep
news.body: Goldman Sachs surged ~9% on a strong Q2 beat; JPMorgan and Bank of America each gained roughly 2%+ after reporting Tuesday — setting a positive tone heading into today's Morgan Stanley and BlackRock prints.

news.head: Iran Strait & Oil
news.body: Trump abandoned the proposed 20% Strait of Hormuz transit fee, replacing it with Gulf-state trade deals; WTI settled above $79/bbl (prior cash close $79.83) and Brent above $84/bbl — off session highs but still elevated on active U.S.-Iran tensions.

news.head: IBM Drags Dow
news.body: IBM fell roughly 25% Tuesday after warning Q2 profits would miss estimates due to soft software and infrastructure demand, single-handedly capping Dow gains to just +0.02%.

news.head: China Trade Data Surges
news.body: China's June exports jumped 27% year-over-year — the fastest since October 2021 — and imports rose 36%, the largest gain since June 2021, with a $125.6 bn trade surplus; markets are watching a late-July Politburo meeting for stimulus signals.

news.head: Fed Chair Warsh — Day 2 Today
news.body: Chair Warsh delivers the second day of his semi-annual congressional testimony today; he reiterated the Fed's inflation-fighting commitment Tuesday without signaling a more aggressive stance, leaving a ~50% chance of a September hike in market pricing.

news.head: Wheat Disruption — Black Sea Shipping Routes Closing
news.body: Russian-Ukrainian shipping paths through the Black Sea are effectively closing, driving Romanian wheat up ~$11/tonne in two days and putting wheat (prior close 644 c/bu, 94th percentile of 3 years) at further upside risk.

implications: A second straight soft inflation print (PPI today after CPI Tuesday) would compress the September hike probability and is the cleanest near-term positive catalyst for rate-sensitive equities and bonds.

Oil is only partly off the boil: WTI (prior close $79.83/bbl) and Brent (prior close $85.34/bbl) remain elevated despite the Hormuz fee reversal — any fresh Middle East escalation is the fastest route to renewed equity-market stress.

Bank earnings momentum is real: Goldman's ~9% pop and broad beats from JPMorgan and BofA validate the bull case; today's Morgan Stanley (consensus ~$2.81 EPS) and BlackRock prints are the next test of whether trading and fee revenue hold up.
IBM's ~25% drop is a reminder that idiosyncratic software/infrastructure risk is live even in a rising market — watch today's JNJ, UAL, and ASML for cross-sector read-throughs.
Gold traded ~$4,050 overnight (prior cash close $4,058.30/oz) — holding CPI-driven gains; real rates at 2.33% are a structural ceiling, but geopolitical demand is keeping a floor under the metal.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile of 3 years) — a contrarian floor for small-caps. Similarly, speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3M SOFR (2nd percentile) — a contrarian-bullish lean for front-end rates if the hike narrative fades. On the other side, speculators are heavily positioned long Copper (94th percentile) — a contrarian warning given copper's already extreme 98th-percentile price level ($6.367/lb prior close). British pound specs are also at a 3-year positioning low — a potential contrarian floor for GBP.

watch.head: 8:30 ET — PPI (June)
watch.body: Consensus expects June headline PPI at -0.1% month-over-month and +6.2% year-over-year; a downside miss following Tuesday's CPI beat could meaningfully reduce September hike odds and provide a second leg to the bond rally.

watch.head: 8:30 ET — Empire State Manufacturing (July)
watch.body: Consensus is 8.6 (prior 5.7); a strong read would bolster the soft-landing case, while a miss would add caution ahead of Thursday's retail sales and Philly Fed.

watch.head: Pre-Open Earnings — MS & BLK
watch.body: Morgan Stanley (consensus ~$2.81 EPS, ~$19.34bn revenue) and BlackRock report before the bell; trading revenue at MS and AUM flows at BlackRock will set the tone for the broader financial sector today.

watch.head: Warsh Day-2 Testimony
watch.body: Any shift in tone from Tuesday — particularly on the threshold for hiking versus holding — is the single highest-impact Fed-communication event remaining this week.

watch.head: 10-Year Yield (prior close 4.58%)
watch.body: Watch whether a soft PPI pulls the 10-year back toward 4.50% — that move is the mechanical trigger for a rotation from value/banks back into rate-sensitive growth and real estate.

watch.head: WTI Crude (prior close $79.83/bbl)
watch.body: Any fresh Strait of Hormuz headline — escalation or de-escalation — will move oil fast and reprice inflation expectations in real time.

watch.head: ASML Earnings (today)
watch.body: As the dominant maker of chipmaking equipment, ASML's net booking numbers are the earliest reliable signal of where semiconductor capital spending heads in late 2026 — critical context for TSM (setup in our scan) reporting Thursday.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: 4.58% (prior cash close); 2-year: 4.18% (prior cash close) — the yield curve is +40 bps steep (10Y minus 2Y), a gentle positive slope that historically reflects early-cycle normalization.

June CPI printed 3.5% year-over-year and -0.4% month-over-month — the first monthly decline since 2020 — with core CPI at 2.6%; both beat expectations and are the strongest near-term argument against a September Fed hike.
Today's June PPI (consensus: -0.1% m/m, +6.2% y/y) is the follow-on test; a second soft print would push the September hike probability — currently around 50% in money markets — materially lower.

Real rates remain at 2.33% (prior close), keeping borrowing costs genuinely restrictive; the 10-year breakeven inflation expectation sits at 2.25%, implying the bond market sees inflation returning toward target but not yet there.
The bond volatility index (MOVE) is at 75 — calm by recent standards — suggesting the rates market is not pricing a large surprise from today's data or Warsh testimony.

Fed Chair Warsh delivers Day 2 of his semi-annual testimony today; Tuesday he reaffirmed price-stability commitment without escalating hawkish rhetoric — markets will parse every word on the hike threshold.

The dollar index (DXY) closed at 100.94 (prior cash close); the yen remains at an extreme 99th-percentile weak reading at 162.18 ¥/$ (prior cash close) — any dovish pivot hint from Warsh is the fastest catalyst for a yen-squeeze reversal.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3M SOFR futures (2nd percentile of the past 3 years, net position -21.2% of open interest, with hedgers at the opposite extreme) — a contrarian-bullish lean for front-end rates. If today's PPI softens, this extended short positioning in rate futures creates squeeze risk — meaning traders who bet against bonds may be forced to cover quickly, pushing bond prices up and yields down.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 prior cash close: 7,543.59 (+0.38% Tuesday); Nasdaq Composite prior cash close: 26,107.01 (+0.90%); Dow Jones prior cash close: 52,508.27 (+0.02%).
Overnight S&P 500 futures are near flat (pre-market level); the prior session's gains were driven by semiconductor stocks rebounding from Monday's sell-off and CPI-fueled risk appetite.
Technology was the standout sector Tuesday (+1.29% SPDR XLK); Health Care (-1.93%) and Consumer Staples (-1.38%) were the biggest drags — defensive rotation reversed as inflation fears eased.

IBM fell roughly 25% Tuesday after a Q2 profit warning citing weak software and infrastructure demand — a company-specific shock, but a reminder that AI spending enthusiasm has not lifted all enterprise tech.
Goldman Sachs popped ~9% on its Q2 beat; JPMorgan and BofA each gained over 2% — bank earnings season is off to a strong start heading into today's Morgan Stanley and BlackRock prints.
Breadth is moderate: 64% of S&P 500 members are above their 50-day moving average and 67.1% above their 200-day (as of Jul 13) — participation is decent but not stretched.

The CAPE ratio stands at 42 — well above long-run averages — meaning valuations price in a great deal of good news; the equity risk premium (extra return stocks offer over bonds) is -2.05%, which means bonds are now offering a better risk-adjusted return than equities on paper.
VIX: 16.5 (prior close) — complacent; SKEW index at 145.1 signals institutional investors are quietly buying tail-risk protection (out-of-the-money puts) despite the low headline fear gauge.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile of 3 years, net position only +2.7% of open interest, with hedgers at the opposite extreme) — a contrarian floor for small-caps. Shorts are heavy in Russell 2000 with meaningful squeeze risk if today's PPI softens and rate-hike odds fall. Large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) is live across multiple setups in our scan including GGAL, AVO, STNG, GLP, SPG, and TSM.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — The world's dominant chip foundry and the single most important read on AI chip demand; reports Thursday with Q2 revenue guided to $39–40.2bn. Large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) is live, a burst of unusual options buying has been flagged, and company insiders have been buying — stock is trading above its 200-day moving average. ASML's bookings today will be the pre-read.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield credit spreads: 269 bps over investment-grade (as of Jul 13) — not distressed, but watch for widening if oil re-accelerates or PPI surprises to the upside.
Investment-grade spreads (OAS): 78 bps (as of Jul 13) — tight, consistent with benign corporate credit conditions.
The HY/IG ETF ratio is 1.3455 (prior close) — holding up, meaning the riskiest corporate bonds are not underperforming safer ones, which is a healthy credit signal.
FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS spreads are both at -2 bps (prior close) — essentially zero, meaning there is no stress in the overnight bank-funding market; plumbing is clean.

Bank reserves at the Fed: $3,098.9bn (as of Jul 8) — ample; the reverse repo facility is nearly drained at just $0.3bn (prior close), which has historically been a signal that excess liquidity is migrating into risk assets and Treasuries.
The Treasury General Account (TGA) holds $774.1bn (as of Jul 8) — any drawdown to fund spending injects reserves into the system, a modest tailwind for liquidity.
Commercial paper spreads (CPFF) at 18 bps and bank credit growing 5.93% year-over-year (as of Jul 1) — no funding stress visible in short-term corporate credit.
M2 money supply is growing 5.58% year-over-year (as of May) — moderate, not reigniting inflation on its own but not restrictive either.

single_name.note: Scorpio Tankers (STNG) — Product tanker operator that benefits directly from elevated oil prices and active Strait of Hormuz shipping rerouting; large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) and a burst of unusual options buying are both live, company insiders have been buying (2 insider rules fired), and the stock is above its 200-day moving average. With shorts covering 2.2 days of average volume, squeeze risk is present if tanker demand stays elevated.
